newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude premia firmer, paper market quiet.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude premia firmer, paper market quiet.

text.p: Asian crude prices were indicating some firmer differentials on Tuesday, with the exception of Indonesian grades, where talk was quiet.
The paper market was quiet. Brent/Dubai and Dubai intermonths were steady but paper Tapis fell.
Paper Tapis levels fell to a notional $19.45/$19.75 per barrel compared with day-earlier levels that were 20 cents higher. October was assessed at 15 cents backwardation.
Traders put the Brent/Dubai market Tuesday at a notional $1.65/$1.73. A U.S. refinery offered the October Brent/Dubai at $1.73. Otherwise discussion was quiet.
But wet Tapis premiums were firmer with a Japanese trader said to have sold two lots of 200,000 barrels to two U.S. majors at premiums ranging 55 to 65 cents from last done at 60.
A September Challis was traded between a producer and a major at Tapis quotes plus 95 cents premium, while 600,000 barrels of Miri crude were traded on a P+C basis.
An Oman trade was said done at Friday at MPM plus four cents, the highest October deal to date.
